In Re: An application for anticipatory bail under Section
 482 of the Bnss, 2023.

In connection with Bowbazar P.S
 case no. 43 of 2022 dated 09/02/2022 under sections
 406/409/420/467/468/120B of the Ipc.

In the matter of: Bharat Bhushan Sunda
 ...Petitioner.
 Mr. Anirban Dutta
 Mr. Raghav Munshi
 Ms. Mohini Majumder
 ...for the petitioner.
 Mr. Anand Keshari
 Ms. Debjani Sahu
 ...for the State.

1.
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits as follows.
In 2010, the HUF property of the petitioner's father was sold.
In the very same year, the de-facto complainant being the sister of the present petitioner filed a partition suit for properties that included the said sold property in question.
The petitioner gave reply in which he mentioned that the property had been sold.
Subsequently, the de-facto complainant filed another partition suit for the properties including the sold out property.

In 2025, after passage of so many years, the de-facto complainant lodged the present FIR alleging that in the deed for the property sold in 2010, the de-facto complainant was not shown as an interest holder.
There is no question of forgery being there.
Even for argument's sake, if there is a document that contains a false information, the same does not tantamount to forgery.
2. Learned counsel appearing for the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail.
He relies on the statements of the witnesses present in the case diary.

3. Considering the above, the other materials available in the case diary and the fact that the allegations levelled also have a civil profile, I do not think that custodial interrogation of the petitioner is required in this case and I am inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

5. Accordingly, the application for anticipatory bail is allowed.
